text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a large dip in KV cache hit rate after the tool param ordering change yesterday.  ~25% fewer prefix hits on canary.
maya: ugh. which change exactly? the JSON field reorder or the escape normalization? :eyes:
sam: Looks like both. The reorder made identical logical prompts produce different raw strings, and our current keyer hashes the raw concatenation.
alex: repro snippet from logs:
```
old_key = join([system_prompt, user_prompt, tools_serialized])
# tools_serialized used stable-ordering=false
```
new_key = join([system_prompt, user_prompt, tools_serialized])
# tools_serialized serialized with field-order-from-client
```
maya: so same semantics, different bytes -> different hash -> miss. makes sense.
julie: Also found tokenizer differences when the system prompt got its trailing newline trimmed by frontend. one side had `\n` suffix, other didn't.
will: packet from profiler: kernel selection went up 8% allocs for the missed-paths because warmup didn't trigger and we fell back to cold kernel with longer preamble.
sam: quick numbers: canary traffic 10k rps, prefix hit rate dropped from 72% -> 54%. token cost rose ~12% and p95 latency +30ms.
alex: proposed quick fixes:
- canonicalize tool serialization (sorted keys + stable escaping)
- normalize system prompt whitespace (strip trailing newlines or force single newline)
- include tokenizer version in cache key metadata
- make a short-term rollout that treats old/new keys as equivalent via dual-hash lookup
maya: dual-hash lookup is safe? costs extra lookups though.
alex: yes extra lookup but only for canary fraction; fallback lookup is cheap compared to cold kernel cost.
sam: I sketched a canonicalizer prototype this morning. example normalization rule:
```
serialize_tools(obj) -> json.dumps(obj, separators=(",",":"), sort_keys=True)
escape_newlines(s) -> s.replace('\r\n','\n')
key_v2 = sha256(tokenizer_version + '\0' + escape_newlines(system) + '\0' + serialize_tools(tools) + '\0' + user_prompt)
```
julie: include tokenizer_version so when we update vocab pin we don't invalidate everything. :+1:
will: i'd also add a short `tool_order_hash` field to the key rather than full serialized tools — reduces key length and normalization cost.
maya: what about function/toolcall positionality? some clients rely on order as semantics.
alex: agreed — we only sort internal metadata fields. we must preserve ordered lists that are semantically ordered (e.g., choices array). only sort object/map fields.
sam: warmup strategy idea: sample top 10k distinct v2 keys from traffic history, and run warmup workers that prefetch KV into local caches across GPU pool during quiet windows.
will: plus tiered eviction: pin v2 keys for 48h after rollout to avoid thrash.
julie: rollout plan:
1) ship canonicalizer in read-only: compute v2 keys and log collisions
2) enable dual-lookup (v1 then v2) for a small canary
3) if metrics good, switch to v2 primary and keep v1 fallback for 7 days
4) drop v1 after 2 weeks
sam: infra-bot: deploy job queued: "kv-keyer-canonicalizer" (eta 12:00 UTC)
infra-bot: Canary rollout ready at 12:15 UTC. monitoring: kv.hit_rate, kernel.cold_fallbacks, p95_latency
maya: we should add an eval to detect semantic-equivalent prompts that still diverge due to quoting; small set of unit cases to avoid regressions.
alex: good call. i'll add a test harness and a few sample tool payloads from logs.
will: also add a metric `kv.dual_lookup_ratio` so we can see how many fell back to v1.
julie: final note: make the key namespace include `keying_version` so older services can ignore unknown keys.
alex: ok I'll open a PR for the canonicalizer + rollout doc. tagging you all. :shipit:
maya: thanks — i'll prepare the warmup worker patch.
sam: i'll run the profiler after canary to validate kernel selection improvements.
infra-bot: canary started at 12:15 UTC — routing 5% traffic to keyer-v2
julie: seeing initial +2% hit rate already on canary. nice.
alex: closing loop tomorrow unless anyone objects.
